description: ACTN-02's behavioural proof, and the fixture owed by CLAUDE.md's 'teach a tool, owe a fixture' rule now that `proposeCalendarEvent` and `checkAvailability` are in the cockpit body at all. Before this change the two tools were fully built in llm.ts (:2376 and :2472) and the body did not mention either one — and because CLAUDE.md §5 forbids a hardcoded prompt there is no fallback instruction path, so a tool absent from the body is a tool the agent cannot be expected to reach. That is the same shape as the clock-plane defect (19-11) and the vault island: built, unit-tested, unreachable. The turn asks in plain calendar grammar and the agent must route it to `proposeCalendarEvent` rather than answering 'I've put that on your calendar', which is a claim no reply assertion can tell apart from success. `calendarEventPresent` is graded off `plan.eventStartMs`, which llm.ts writes at EXACTLY ONE site — the `resolved` branch of that tool — and plans.ts clears on reset, so a finite value cannot arrive by any other path; it also pins the resolved branch specifically, because the ambiguous/past/tooFar/none branches all return their refusal prose WITHOUT patching the row. THE TIME PHRASE IS LOAD-BEARING AND WAS CHOSEN AGAINST THE PARSER, NOT BY FEEL: `parseSendTime`'s weekday anchor computes `deltaDays = (dow - nowDow + 7) % 7` and rewrites a zero to 7, so 'Thursday at 2pm' is ALWAYS in the future — on a Thursday it means next Thursday — and 7 days sits far inside `CALENDAR_HORIZON_MS` (365 days). A bare 'at 2' would have been rejected as ambiguous and a bare AM time with no day likewise, so either would have measured the parser instead of the body, and 'today at 2pm' would have been PAST for every gate run after 14:00 UTC — a fixture that reddens by wall-clock is worse than no fixture. `clock: true` is required, not cosmetic: `proposeCalendarEvent` returns its no-clientContext refusal before it ever reaches the parser, so without a clock this fixture would measure the missing clock (the fixture-36 precedent, and the 19-11 defect verbatim). `recipientCount: 0` and `attachmentCount: 0` are the anti-drift teeth 35/36/37 use, and they are not decorative here: fixture 36 measured this exact model reframing a records request into an outbound email twice at $0.0115, so a calendar ask that quietly becomes a compose must be red. `statusAtMost: proposed` pins that staging never silently applies past the human Approve gate — the create happens in `calendar.createEvent` after Approve and this harness never clicks it, so a staged event is never evidence anything reached a real calendar. DELIBERATELY ONE TURN. A second turn giving an ambiguous time — the obvious 'it must ask instead of guessing' companion — WOULD BE VACUOUS HERE and was not written: `patchPlan` overwrites `eventStartMs` wholesale, so a turn-2 stage and a turn-2 refusal both leave the field finite and `calendarEventPresent` cannot tell them apart. That is the replacement-satisfies-the-count hole 19-11 found in fixture 36, recognised in advance rather than after a paid run. The refusal branches are covered OFFLINE instead, at $0, by the runner's own self-check 2j, which asserts an absent and a non-finite start both grade RED. A `checkAvailability` companion is also deliberately absent: it calls the provider, the eval tenant has no connected calendar, so it can only ever exercise the reconnect path and would assert nothing about routing. What would make this vacuous, and is therefore NOT done: naming the TOOL in the turn ('block out ... on my calendar' is the domain grammar the product and the body both use, not a tool name); asserting only `statusAtMost`, which every fixture in the set already satisfies; or asserting `planKind: calendar_event`, which reads the same patch but is paired by validateFixture with `actOnGap` under 15-06's gap-dispatch-only rule and would be rejected before the first spawn. NOTE ON THE OTHER HALF OF THIS CHANGE: the same commit merges the body's `Attachments` and `Creating a document or a post` sections into one. That half teaches NO new tool, so it owes no new fixture — fixtures 10, 11, 12 and 35 already exercise `generateAttachment`, `regenerateAttachment`, `removeAttachment` and `createDocument`, and they are the regression signal for the merge. If the restructuring degrades attachment or document routing, those four redden, which is exactly the intended alarm.
turns: Block out an hour on my calendar for Thursday at 2pm — the benchmark-CAL7 pricing review.
